messages:
Maya: FYI a customer asked for 'trace-linked billing' — basically surface cost per-tenant in Console and link to traces so SREs can investigate expensive requests. They want minimal SDK changes.
Liam: Important: are they expecting exact billing numbers or an engineer-friendly estimate?
Maya: They asked for estimates that are 'good enough to flag hot customers' and be able to jump to the trace for post-mortem. Not legal-grade billing.
Priya: Implementation idea: emit two fields on span root: `cost_estimated` (float) and `cost_flags` (enum: "high", "normal"). Also tag spans with `tenant_hash`, `route`, `model`. Dashboard aggregates by those tags.
Noah: Sampling policy: default sample rate stays low (1%). Add a dynamic sampler that forces 100% for spans with cost_estimated > $Y or when tenant is in canary set. That avoids missing expensive tails.
Zoe: UX: dashboard should have "Top spenders (est.)" table, ability to pivot by model/route, timepicker, and a button to "Open trace" which navigates to trace explorer and highlights the cost-related spans.
Dina: Launch criteria proposal: 1) Dashboard with tenant/model/route pivot and drilldowns; 2) Traces open from dashboard with cost tags visible; 3) Export opt-in to BigQuery with defined schema; 4) Docs + migration/opt-in guide.
Liam: About schema and export: propose simple export rows: `event_ts, tenant_hash, model, route, tokens_est, cost_est, trace_id, billing_window_id`. Keep types stable. I can own schema and version it.
Priya: SDK change surface: add optional `obs_metadata` to request payload. Offer shim so older SDKs still work. Languages: py/ts/go first. Snippet:
```
obs = {"model":"redwood-amt-2b", "route":"/v1/chat"}
client.request(prompt, obs_metadata=obs)
span.set_tag('cost_estimated', 0.0045)
```
Maya: Nice. Any infra blockers? Noah?
Noah: Two: 1) tracing ingestion throughput needs a small increase for high-sample canaries; 2) storage cost if we retain 100% traces for many customers. We'll need to cap retention for non-canary tenants. Estimate infra work 6-8 dev-days.
Zoe: Metrics to measure success: accuracy (median delta between est vs billing) < 15% for top 50 tenants, reduction in time-to-detect expensive regressions by 50% in canary trials, and <250ms median dashboard query latency.
Dina: Privacy/legal: storing `tenant_hash` is ok but must avoid PII. Exports disabled by default; enable only on signed agreements. I'll prep the legal checklist.
Liam: Operational concerns: Add feature flag gating, rate-limiting on console queries, and audit logs for exports. Also add a reconciliation job that compares estimates vs invoice and flags >10% deltas.
Priya: Dev plan: Phase 0 (hotfix) add `model` and `route` tags to spans. Phase 1 (MVP) add cost_estimated tags + dashboard and internal export. Phase 2 GA add opt-in BigQuery exports and SDK ergonomics.
Maya: Timeline? Can we do an internal canary (2 customers) in 6 weeks?
Priya: Roughly: Phase 0 = 1 week, Phase 1 = 3w backend + 2w UI = 5w parallel, infra tweaks 1w, so 6-7w to internal canary.
Noah: We should also instrument a billing reconciliation metric during canary to validate the estimator.
Dina: I'll coordinate launch checklist owners: Maya (PM), Priya (SDK/backend), Noah (infra), Liam (export/schema), Zoe (UX), Legal (me).
Maya: OK assigning. Also add runbooks: how to disable high-sample path if costs spike.
Liam: +1 on runbook. And let's add a small beta survey for customers after canary to capture confusions.
Priya: Small engineering note: annotate traces with `batch_id` so we can reconcile when aggregation changes tokenization.
Zoe: UI detail: highlight cost-estimate provenance; tooltip: "Estimate computed at request time; final billed amount may differ due to batching/discounts."
Maya: Great. I'll spin up a short design doc and a meeting to scope epics. Thanks everyone.
observability-bot: Action created OBS-734 "Trace-linked cost view + export opt-in" assigned to Maya, Priya, Noah, Liam, Zoe, Dina.
